verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is publicly readable. It has a GitHub repo, a documented free self-hosted deployment, and users report reading the code to understand integrations. However, community evidence says the core is licensed under the BSL (source-available), not an open-source license, with only older versions or components like Symbolicator described as open source. Missing for 10: an OSI-approved open license for the current core codebase, and first-party license documentation in the evidence.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Sentry is source-available under the BSL; you can still run it for your company for free
The open source code let them see exactly what was happening for advanced integrations instead of relying on docs
How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
competitors such as Embrace use Sentry's open-source Symbolicator
